title: दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुरको कर आधारमै छेडखानीको आशंका, प्राधिकरणको सूचनाले राज्यलाई अर्बौँ राजस्व गुम्ने जोखिम
content:
No ads found for this position काठमाडौं । नेपाल दूरसञ्चार प्राधिकरणले इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायक (आईएसपी) हरूसँग दूरसञ्चार सेवा दस्तुर (टीएससी) को विवरण माग गर्दै जारी गरेको सार्वजनिक सूचनामा करको आधार स्रोतमाथि नै छेडखानी गर्न खोजिएको गम्भीर आशंका उब्जिएको छ। प्राधिकरणले मंसिर २ गते (२०८३।०८।०२) १० कार्यदिनभित्र आर्थिक वर्ष २०८२/८३ र चालु आर्थिक वर्षको असोज महिनासम्मको टीएससीसम्बन्धी विवरण पेस गर्न इन्टरनेट (इमेलसहित) सेवा प्रदायकहरूलाई सूचना जारी गरेको थियो। आर्थिक ऐन, २०८३ को दफा ८ को उपदफा ५ बमोजिम टीएससी प्रशासन प्राधिकरणले निर्धारण गरेबमोजिम हुने व्यवस्था टेकेर उक्त सूचना प्रकाशित गरिएको हो। तर, प्राधिकरणले मागेको विवरणको ढाँचामा मर्मत-सम्भार बापतको ‘आम्दानी’ मात्र खुलाउन भनिएको र ‘वास्तविक खर्च’ (Actual Cost of Support and Maintenance) नमागिएकाले नीतिगत रूपमै राजस्व छलीलाई वैधता दिन खोजिएको आशंका गरिएको हो। कहाँ छ मुख्य कैफियत र अनियमितताको आशंका ? दूरसञ्चार ऐन, २०५३, नियमावली, २०५४ र आर्थिक वर्ष २०७५/७६ देखिका आर्थिक ऐनहरूले फिक्स्ड ब्रोडब्यान्ड सेवामा मर्मत–सम्भार बापत उपभोक्ताबाट लिइने मासिक महसुलको अधिकतम ५० प्रतिशतसम्मको रकममा टीएससी नलाग्ने व्यवस्था गरेको छ। कानुनी व्यवस्थाअनुसार सेवा प्रदायकले मर्मत–सम्भारमा गरेको वास्तविक खर्च मा मात्र टीएससी छुट पाउने स्पष्ट छ। तर, अधिकांश इन्टरनेट सेवा प्रदायकहरूको वार्षिक मर्मत–सम्भार खर्च कुल आम्दानीको ४ देखि ७ प्रतिशत (अधिकतम ७ प्रतिशत) मात्र हुने गरेको छ। वास्तविक खर्च यति न्यून हुँदाहुँदै पनि सेवा प्रदायकहरूले उपभोक्तालाई बिलिङ गर्दा इन्टरनेट सेवा शुल्ककै १०० प्रतिशत बराबरको रकम मर्मत–सम्भार शीर्षकमा उठाएको देखाउँदै आएका छन्। यसरी कृत्रिम रूपमा आम्दानीलाई खण्डित गरी टीएससीको कर आधार (Tax Base) नै घटाएर राज्यलाई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ राजस्व हानी–नोक्सानी पुर्‍याएको ठूला करदाता कार्यालय र आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागको छानबिनबाट समेत पुष्टि भइसकेको छ। छानबिनबाट स्थापित उक्त बक्यौता तथा जरिवाना असुलउपर गर्न उदासीन देखिएको प्राधिकरणले अहिले वास्तविक खर्च नमागी सेवा प्रदायकले स्वघोषणा गरेको मर्मत–सम्भार आयमै टीएससी छुट दिने गरी विवरण मागेको भन्दै प्रश्न उठाइएको हो। सूचनामा सबै दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायक नसमेटिएकोमा आपत्ति प्राधिकरणले जारी गरेको सूचनामा सबै प्रकारका दूरसञ्चार सेवा प्रदायकलाई नसमेटेर इन्टरनेट (इमेलसहित) सेवा प्रदायकलाई मात्र लक्षित गरिएको प्रति समेत सेवा प्रदायकहरूले आपत्ति जनाएका छन्। आर्थिक ऐनले आ.व. २०७५/७६ देखि नै समग्र दूरसञ्चार सेवा शुल्कमा टीएससी लगाउँदै आएको अवस्थामा एउटा क्षेत्रलाई मात्र लक्षित गरी सूचना निकाल्दा कानुनी व्यवस्थाको हेक्का नराखिएको देखिएको छ। कस्तो विवरण मागिनुपर्थ्यो ? कर आधारमा छेडखानी हुन नदिन र राज्यको राजस्व जोगाउन प्राधिकरणले मासिक बिक्री तथा दाखिला विवरणसँगै निम्नलिखित महत्त्वपूर्ण विवरणहरू अनिवार्य रूपमा माग्नुपर्ने देखिन्छ । मर्मत–सम्भार बापतको वास्तविक खर्च (रु.): सेवा प्रदायकले मर्मत–सम्भारमा वास्तवमै कति खर्च गरे भन्ने प्रमाणित विवरण। बाँकी रहेको टीएससी रकम (रु.): तिर्नुपर्ने कुल टीएससीमध्ये दाखिला हुन बाँकी रहेको बक्यौता रकम। जरिवानाको बक्यौता रकम (रु.): तोकिएको समयभन्दा ढिलो बुझाएको टीएससी बापत मासिक ५ प्रतिशतका दरले लाग्ने जरिवानामध्ये बुझाउन बाँकी रकम। [1] आर्थिक ऐनले वास्तविक खर्चमा मात्र छुट दिएको जगजाहेर रहँदारहँदै आईएसपीहरूले स्वघोषणा गरेको १०० प्रतिशत मर्मत-सम्भार शुल्कमा छुट दिने प्रपञ्च रचिए राज्यलाई अर्बौँ रुपैयाँ टीएससी राजस्व गुम्ने जोखिम देखिएको छ। साथै, ७ प्रतिशत पनि खर्च नहुने शीर्षकमा उपभोक्ताबाट १०० प्रतिशत शुल्क असुलेर सेवा प्रदायकहरूले ग्राहकमाथि समेत दोहोरो शोषण गरिरहेको तथ्य बाहिरिएको छ। Kathmandu. The Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) has issued a public notice requesting details of telecommunications service charges (TSC) from Internet Service Providers (ISPs), raising serious suspicions that the tax base itself is being tampered with. The Authority had issued a notice to internet (including email) service providers on Mangsir 2 (2083.08.02) to submit TSC related details for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year up to Asho month within 10 working days. The notice has been published in accordance with the provisions of Sub-section 5 of Section 8 of the Finance Act, 2083, as determined by the TSC Administration Authority. However, since the format of the details requested by the authority only asks for 'income' from maintenance and repair and does not ask for 'actual cost of support and maintenance', it is suspected that an attempt is being made to legitimize revenue evasion as a policy. Where are the main objections and suspicions of irregularities? The Telecommunications Act, 2053, Regulations, 2054 and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76 have made provision for TSC exemption on a maximum amount of 50 percent of the monthly fee charged from the consumer for maintenance and repair of fixed broadband services. According to the legal provisions, it is clear that the service provider will be exempted from TSC only on the actual expenses incurred by the service provider for maintenance and repair. However, the annual maintenance expenses of most Internet service providers are only 4 to 7 percent (maximum 7 percent) of total revenue. Despite the fact that the actual expenses are so low, service providers have been showing that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance when billing consumers. The investigation by the Large Taxpayers' Office and the Internal Revenue Department has confirmed that the state has lost billions of rupees in revenue by artificially fragmenting income and reducing the tax base of TSC. The Authority, which appears indifferent to recovering the arrears and fines established by the investigation, has now asked for details of TSC exemption on the self-declared maintenance income of the service provider, without asking for actual expenses. Objection to not including all telecommunication service providers in the notification Service providers have also objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers, excluding all types of telecommunications service providers. While the Finance Act has been imposing TSC on the overall telecommunications service fee since FY 2075/76, issuing a notice targeting only one sector has shown disregard for the legal provisions. What details should have been requested? To prevent tax base manipulation and protect state revenue, the Authority must mandatorily request the following important details along with monthly sales and deposit statements. Actual maintenance cost (Rs.): A verified statement of how much the service provider actually spent on maintenance. Outstanding TSC Amount (Rs.): The outstanding amount of TSC due that is yet to be paid. Outstanding amount of fine (Rs.): The amount remaining to be paid out of the 5 percent monthly penalty for late payment of TSC. [1] While it is clear that the Finance Act provides exemption only for actual expenses, if ISPs create a scheme to exempt 100 percent maintenance fees that they have declared themselves, the state is at risk of losing billions of rupees in TSC revenue. In addition, it has been revealed that service providers are doubly exploiting customers by charging 100 percent fees from consumers on the pretext of not spending even 7 percent.

The Authority had issued a notice to internet (including email) service providers on Mangsir 2 (2083.08.02) to submit TSC related details for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year up to Asho month within 10 working days. The notice has been published in accordance with the provisions of Sub-section 5 of Section 8 of the Finance Act, 2083, as determined by the TSC Administration Authority. However, since the format of the details requested by the authority only asks for 'income' from maintenance and repair and does not ask for 'actual cost of support and maintenance', it is suspected that an attempt is being made to legitimize revenue evasion as a policy. Where are the main objections and suspicions of irregularities? The Telecommunications Act, 2053, Regulations, 2054 and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76 have made provision for TSC exemption on a maximum amount of 50 percent of the monthly fee charged from the consumer for maintenance and repair of fixed broadband services. According to the legal provisions, it is clear that the service provider will be exempted from TSC only on the actual expenses incurred by the service provider for maintenance and repair. However, the annual maintenance expenses of most Internet service providers are only 4 to 7 percent (maximum 7 percent) of total revenue. Despite the fact that the actual expenses are so low, service providers have been showing that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance when billing consumers. The investigation by the Large Taxpayers' Office and the Internal Revenue Department has confirmed that the state has lost billions of rupees in revenue by artificially fragmenting income and reducing the tax base of TSC. The Authority, which appears indifferent to recovering the arrears and fines established by the investigation, has now asked for details of TSC exemption on the self-declared maintenance income of the service provider, without asking for actual expenses. Objection to not including all telecommunication service providers in the notification Service providers have also objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers, excluding all types of telecommunications service providers. While the Finance Act has been imposing TSC on the overall telecommunications service fee since FY 2075/76, issuing a notice targeting only one sector has shown disregard for the legal provisions. What details should have been requested? To prevent tax base manipulation and protect state revenue, the Authority must mandatorily request the following important details along with monthly sales and deposit statements. Actual maintenance cost (Rs.): A verified statement of how much the service provider actually spent on maintenance. Outstanding TSC Amount (Rs.): The outstanding amount of TSC due that is yet to be paid. Outstanding amount of fine (Rs.): The amount remaining to be paid out of the 5 percent monthly penalty for late payment of TSC. [1] While it is clear that the Finance Act provides exemption only for actual expenses, if ISPs create a scheme to exempt 100 percent maintenance fees that they have declared themselves, the state is at risk of losing billions of rupees in TSC revenue. In addition, it has been revealed that service providers are doubly exploiting customers by charging 100 percent fees from consumers on the pretext of not spending even 7 percent.

Kathmandu. The Nepal Telecommunication Authority (NTA) has issued a public notice requesting details of telecommunications service charges (TSC) from Internet Service Providers (ISPs), raising serious suspicions that the tax base itself is being tampered with. The Authority had issued a notice to internet (including email) service providers on Mangsir 2 (2083.08.02) to submit TSC related details for the fiscal year 2082/83 and the current fiscal year up to Asho month within 10 working days. The notice has been published in accordance with the provisions of Sub-section 5 of Section 8 of the Finance Act, 2083, as determined by the TSC Administration Authority. However, since the format of the details requested by the authority only asks for 'income' from maintenance and repair and does not ask for 'actual cost of support and maintenance', it is suspected that an attempt is being made to legitimize revenue evasion as a policy. Where are the main objections and suspicions of irregularities? The Telecommunications Act, 2053, Regulations, 2054 and the Financial Acts since the fiscal year 2075/76 have made provision for TSC exemption on a maximum amount of 50 percent of the monthly fee charged from the consumer for maintenance and repair of fixed broadband services. According to the legal provisions, it is clear that the service provider will be exempted from TSC only on the actual expenses incurred by the service provider for maintenance and repair. However, the annual maintenance expenses of most Internet service providers are only 4 to 7 percent (maximum 7 percent) of total revenue. Despite the fact that the actual expenses are so low, service providers have been showing that they have collected 100 percent of the Internet service fee as maintenance when billing consumers. The investigation by the Large Taxpayers' Office and the Internal Revenue Department has confirmed that the state has lost billions of rupees in revenue by artificially fragmenting income and reducing the tax base of TSC. The Authority, which appears indifferent to recovering the arrears and fines established by the investigation, has now asked for details of TSC exemption on the self-declared maintenance income of the service provider, without asking for actual expenses. Objection to not including all telecommunication service providers in the notification Service providers have also objected to the fact that the notice issued by the Authority targets only Internet (including email) service providers, excluding all types of telecommunications service providers. While the Finance Act has been imposing TSC on the overall telecommunications service fee since FY 2075/76, issuing a notice targeting only one sector has shown disregard for the legal provisions. What details should have been requested? To prevent tax base manipulation and protect state revenue, the Authority must mandatorily request the following important details along with monthly sales and deposit statements. Actual maintenance cost (Rs.): A verified statement of how much the service provider actually spent on maintenance. Outstanding TSC Amount (Rs.): The outstanding amount of TSC due that is yet to be paid. Outstanding amount of fine (Rs.): The amount remaining to be paid out of the 5 percent monthly penalty for late payment of TSC. [1] While it is clear that the Finance Act provides exemption only for actual expenses, if ISPs create a scheme to exempt 100 percent maintenance fees that they have declared themselves, the state is at risk of losing billions of rupees in TSC revenue. In addition, it has been revealed that service providers are doubly exploiting customers by charging 100 percent fees from consumers on the pretext of not spending even 7 percent.
